title: New to Game Making: Should I buy MV or MZ ?

posts.author: dwr7eleven
posts.body:
I've wanted to make a game for the longest time, and I heared that RPG Maker was a great place for beginners!
The game I want to make is a spiritual successor to (or to be more frank, a nightmare mode version of) The Mario & Luigi Franchise. I plan to have it feature:
* The same Mario & Luigi combat system you know and love!
* A Pokémon Type Effectiveness Chart, but with different strengths and weaknesses!
* The dearly beloved, but for some reason underused scrolling HP bar mechanic from the Earthbound/Mother series, and maybe the Rythm Heartbeat Mechanic too, if it will work with the main combat system.
* Original Story with dangerous monsters and threatening villains!
* Unbearable status conditions that make the game harder than it already is!
* PERMADEATH! You can save the game, but once everyone's HP reaches zero, all of your saves are deleted. YES, ALL OF THEM!
The issue is, what game engine should I choose? MV or MZ? I also know that the engines go on sale a lot, so should I buy them both if they go on sale?

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
First thing, you should download both trials and test them to see what you can work with.
That said, MV and MZ are mostly identical with MZ being the newer engine that has some upgrades.
Most impotant of them are manual layering and added particle animations.
MV on the other hand is older, which means it had more time to accumulate community work/additions.
There is also a trend to more obfuscated and more paid plugins with MZ, there are more free and open plugins with MV.

Actual answer to the thread: MV due to its wealth of legacy content and plugins.
But um...

Who is your target audience, dawg?
LIke, what's the point of the heartbeat combos from Mother 3 if you're already doing M&L action commands (which already involve you pressing buttons to deal more damage or dodge). Also, the rolling HP would be pointless if you're wasting time to do action commands - it works in EB/Mother 3 because everything is otherwise static turn-based combat.
I get you want the game to be hard, but like... again, who is your audience? The super hardcore kaizo difficulty romhack speedrunners? Because that's a very small niche to appeal to, especially without a prior audience - most everyone else would probably get frustrated quickly and stop playing, maybe even refund if they find the design especially annoying or cheap.
Just my two cents.

I didn't really come up with the idea for a game with a target audience in mind. I was just playing Mario & Luigi one day and thought, "Hmm, what if it was harder? What if it had the Pokemon Type chart, and one that actually made sense at that?"
Maybe the rhythm mechanic from Mother 3 wouldn't be the best idea, but I think the scrolling numbers mechanic would be crucial for a game like this. In a game with permadeath (especially in a game with no reviving items), it would give the player tension, but also a chance to spare their character. It would make devious boss fights all the more impactful, memorable, talked about. People would make comics about this. About how they almost died, or how soul crushing it is to lose their in-game friend, if only they were to heal their friend in time.
Come to think of it, maybe I do have a target audience. Maybe my target audience is masochistic, nuzelocke-obsessed fans of Mario & Luigi like myself. Obviously, I would HEAVILY advertise the game as "HARD GAME, ALERT! IF YOU DO NOT LIKE PAIN, THIS GAME IS NOT FOR YOU!", but I wouldn't want the game to feel cheap. I know there are people out there who like painfully difficult games. Not just free games like Sybon-Action (A.K.A. Cat Mario), but I know that people would pay for games like Dark Souls, Hollow Knight, and quite possibly the greatest example, Fear and Hunger! (A game that costs money, is Sticker Star levels of painful but in a good way, and was made in RPG Maker MV.) I'm aware that my game isn't meant to be horror, and I am also aware that people are meant to engage with the combat (unlike with Fear & Hunger and Sticker Star).
With all this in mind, I will not include the Heartbeat Rhythm mechanic. I do not plan to make my game like Fear & Hunger or Sticker Star, but I do plan to make it painfully difficult without it being unfair.
